t: Find the Substring With Maximum Cost — Kadane with Custom Values
o: Assign each letter a value (custom if in chars, else alphabet position), then find the maximum-sum substring — exactly Kadane's algorithm, allowing the empty substring (answer at least 0). Example 1: 'd' costs -1000, so best is "aa" = 2. Example 2: all values -1, so the empty substring wins with 0. Build a value lookup table once, then a single O(|s|) pass.
k: Map characters to values upfront (hash map or 26-array), then the problem reduces to maximum subarray sum.
Kadane with reset-at-negative handles the empty-substring allowance by clamping the running sum at 0.

a.i: Keep a running sum; after each character, if the running sum drops below 0, reset to 0 (start fresh). Track the maximum seen, initialized to 0 so the empty substring is covered.
s: Build value map from chars/vals; default ord(c)-96.
Scan s: add the character's value to cur; clamp cur to max(cur, 0); update ans.
a.t: O(|s| + |chars|) — table build plus one linear scan

w: Recognizing the Kadane pattern instantly is the point of the problem. Pitfalls: forgetting the empty substring floor of 0 (initialize ans = 0), and miscomputing default alphabet values (1-indexed). Follow-up: return the substring itself, or handle updates to vals (segment tree over values with max-prefix queries).
